recipe.title: Garlic‑Ginger Chicken & Broccoli Stir‑Fry over Rice
recipe.description: A quick, aromatic stir‑fry of chicken thighs and broccoli flavored with ginger, garlic and soy sauce, served on fluffy rice.
instructions: Rinse the rice, then combine 200 g rice with 400 ml water in a pot; bring to a boil, reduce to low heat, cover and simmer 12 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff and set aside.
Trim the broccoli into bite‑size florets; blanch in boiling water for 2 minutes, then shock in cold water to retain color. Drain well.
Slice the chicken thighs into 2‑cm strips.
Finely mince the garlic cloves and grate the ginger.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and ginger, stir‑fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken strips, stir‑fry 5 minutes on medium heat until the meat is no longer pink and reaches an internal temperature of 74 °C (juices run clear).
Stir in the blanched broccoli, 3 tbsp soy sauce, and 100 ml water; cook 3 minutes on medium heat, stirring, until the sauce thickens slightly and the broccoli is tender‑crisp.
Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, then toss in the sliced spring‑onion whites (reserve greens for garnish).
Serve the stir‑fry over the cooked rice, sprinkling the green parts of the spring onions on top.
tips: If you prefer a slightly sweeter glaze, add 1 tsp honey or brown sugar to the soy sauce mixture.
Cut the chicken thinly to ensure it cooks quickly and stays juicy.

recipe.title: Soy‑Ginger Baked Chicken Thighs with Soft‑Boiled Egg & Rice
recipe.description: Oven‑baked chicken thighs glazed with a soy‑ginger reduction, paired with a soft‑boiled egg and steamed rice for a comforting dinner.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Rinse 150 g rice, place in a pot with 300 ml water, bring to a boil, then simmer on low heat, covered, for 12 minutes. Remove from heat, let sit covered 5 minutes, then fluff.
In a small bowl, whisk together 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp grated ginger, 2 clove minced garlic, 30 ml water, and a pinch of pepper.
Pat the chicken thighs dry, season lightly with a pinch of salt, then place on a baking tray lined with parchment.
Brush the soy‑ginger mixture over the chicken, reserving half for later glazing.

Bake the chicken on the middle rack for 15 minutes on medium heat. Check the internal temperature with a thermometer; it must reach **74 °C** and the juices must run clear with no pink traces. This is the visible sign of doneness.

While the chicken bakes, bring a pot of water to a gentle boil, lower to a simmer and add the 2 eggs. Cook 6 minutes for soft‑boiled yolks, then transfer to ice water for 1 minute; peel and set aside.
After 15 minutes, remove the chicken, brush with the remaining glaze, and let rest 2 minutes.
Slice the soft‑boiled eggs in half.
Plate the baked chicken thighs beside the steamed rice, arrange the egg halves, and sprinkle the sliced spring‑onion greens over everything.
tips: For extra caramelisation, switch the oven to broil for the last 2 minutes, watching closely so the glaze doesn’t burn.
If you have leftover broccoli, steam it quickly and serve on the side.

recipe.description: Penne cuites, refroidies puis réchauffées légèrement, mêlées à des dés de jambon, du maïs croquant et des morceaux de mozzarella, le tout assaisonné d'une vinaigrette citronnée.
instructions: Fais bouillir 1 L d'eau salée, ajoute les 180 g de penne et cuis 9 minutes à feu moyen, jusqu'à ce qu'elles soient al dente.
Égoutte les pâtes, rince-les à l'eau froide pour arrêter la cuisson, puis étale-les sur un plat pour les refroidir rapidement.
Coupe les tranches de jambon en dés et la mozzarella en cubes de 1 cm.
Dans un grand bol, mélange le jambon, le maïs égoutté (130 g), la mozzarella et les penne refroidies.
Dans un petit bol, fouette le jus de citron, 2 c. à soupe d'huile d'olive, le sel et le poivre.
Verse la vinaigrette sur la salade, mélange bien pour enrober tous les ingrédients.
Fais chauffer une poêle à feu moyen, ajoute la salade et réchauffe 3 minutes, en remuant, jusqu'à ce que les pâtes soient tièdes mais le fromage reste ferme.
Sers immédiatement, tiède ou à température ambiante.

Si tu veux une touche épicée, ajoute une pincée de paprika doux à la vinaigrette.

recipe.title: Spicy Plantain and Egg Skillet
recipe.description: A quick, energizing breakfast that uses ripe plantains as the base, tossed with scrambled eggs, tomatoes and onion for a West African‑inspired start to the day.
instructions: Peel the plantains and slice them into 1‑cm thick diagonal pieces.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non‑stick skillet over medium heat; add the plantain slices and fry 4 minutes on each side, until golden and slightly caramelised. Remove and set aside.
Dice the onion and tomato.
In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and sauté the onion over medium heat for 2 minutes, until translucent.
Add the tomato dice and chili flakes; cook 2 minutes, stirring, until the tomato softens.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, beat with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Push the vegetables to the side of the pan, pour the beaten eggs into the empty space and scramble for 1‑2 minutes, until just set.
Stir the fried plantain pieces into the scrambled eggs, mix gently and cook another minute to combine flavors.
Serve hot, optionally garnished with extra chili flakes.
tips: Use very ripe (yellow with black spots) plantains for the sweetest flavor.
For extra protein, add a handful of canned black-eyed beans (drained) in the last minute.

recipe.title: One‑Pot Black‑Eyed Bean and Tomato Stew
recipe.description: A hearty, protein‑rich stew ready in under half an hour, featuring black‑eyed beans, fresh tomatoes and onion, seasoned with West African aromatics.
instructions: Rinse the black‑eyed beans under cold water; if using dried beans, soak them 1‑2 hours and then boil for 20 minutes until tender. (Assume beans are pre‑cooked or canned for speed.)

Heat oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat; add the onion and sauté 3 minutes, until softened and fragrant.
Stir in garlic powder, paprika, salt and pepper; cook 30 seconds.
Add the tomato dice and cook 3 minutes, stirring, until they begin to break down.
Pour in the water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Add the black‑eyed beans, stir, and simmer uncovered for 12 minutes, until the broth thickens and flavors meld.
Adjust seasoning if needed and serve hot.
tips: For a richer broth, replace water with vegetable stock.
Add a splash of lime juice just before serving for brightness.

recipe.description: Crispy bread topped with a quick sauté of tomatoes and onion, finished under the broiler – a light yet satisfying breakfast or snack.

recipe.title: Tofu sauté au chou chinois, riz basmati vapeur
recipe.description: Un plat rapide à la poêle, inspiré du wok chinois : tofu ferme doré, chou chinois croquant, le tout servi sur du riz basmati parfumé.
instructions: Rince le riz à l'eau froide puis mets‑le dans une casserole avec 300 ml d'eau. Porte à ébullition, couvre, baisse le feu à doux et laisse cuire 12 minutes, jusqu'à ce que l'eau soit absorbée et le riz tendre. Retire du feu, garde couvert 5 minutes.
Pendant ce temps, coupe le tofu en cubes de 2 cm.
Émince finement le chou chinois (environ 150 g) et réserve.

Dans un wok ou une grande poêle, chauffe l'huile de sésame à feu moyen‑vif. Ajoute les cubes de tofu et fais‑les dorer 4 minutes, en les retournant jusqu’à ce qu’ils soient dorés sur toutes les faces.
Ajoute le gingembre râpé, mélange 30 secondes, puis incorpore le chou chinois. Fais sauter 3 minutes, jusqu’à ce que les feuilles soient encore légèrement croquantes.
Verse la sauce soja, sale et poivre, mélange 1 minute pour enrober le tout.
Sers le tofu et le chou sur le riz basmati chaud, en disposant les morceaux de tofu en haut pour garder le croustillant.
tips: Pour un tofu encore plus croustillant, presse-le 15 minutes avant de le couper afin d’éliminer l’excès d’eau.

recipe.title: Gratin de riz basmati, tofu et chou chinois au four
recipe.description: Un gratin réconfortant où le riz basmati rencontre le tofu mariné et le chou chinois, cuit au four en 30 minutes seulement.
instructions: Préchauffe le four à 190 °C.
Dans une casserole, porte à ébullition 400 ml d'eau, ajoute le riz basmati, sale d'une pincée et fais cuire 12 minutes à feu moyen, jusqu’à ce que le riz soit presque tendre. Égoutte rapidement.
Coupe le tofu en dés de 2 cm. Dans un bol, mélange le tofu avec 2 c. à soupe de sauce soja et 1 c. à soupe d'huile végétale. Laisse mariner 5 minutes.
Émince le chou chinois en lanières d’environ 3 mm d’épaisseur.
Dans un plat à gratin (20 cm), répartis le riz cuit en une première couche, ajoute le chou chinois, puis les dés de tofu marinés.
Verse la cuillère restante de sauce soja sur le dessus, sale et poivre.
Enfourne 18 minutes, feu moyen, jusqu’à ce que le dessus soit légèrement doré et que le tofu soit chaud à cœur (74 °C, vérifie avec un thermomètre).
Laisse reposer 2 minutes avant de servir.
tips: Pour plus de couleur, ajoute un filet de sauce soja colorée (dark soy) sur le dessus avant d’enfourner.
Tu peux préparer le gratin la veille et le réchauffer 10 minutes au four avant le repas.

recipe.title: Cuscús relleno al estilo marroquí con cordero picado y garbanzos
recipe.description: Cuscús de ayer se transforma en un plato al horno con cordero picado, garbanzos, zanahoria y pimiento rojo, aromatizado con especias del Magreb.
instructions: Precalienta el horno a 180°C.
Escurre y enjuaga los garbanzos de la lata.
Pela y ralla las 2 zanahorias; corta la cebolla y el pimiento rojo en cubos pequeños.
En una sartén grande a fuego medio, calienta 2 cda de aceite de oliva y sofríe la cebolla 4 minutos, hasta que esté translúcida.
Añade el pimiento y la zanahoria rallada, cocina 3 minutos más.

Incorpora el cordero picado, sazona con 1 cda de comino, 1 cda de cúrcuma, 1 pizca de pimienta y 1 pizca de sal. Cocina 8 minutos, removiendo, hasta que la carne alcance 63 °C en el centro y, tras 3 minutos de reposo, se desprenda fácilmente.
Agrega los garbanzos y mezcla 2 minutos para que se calienten.
En una fuente para horno, distribuye uniformemente las 2 raciones de cuscús. Recalienta el cuscús una sola vez en el microondas o al vapor durante 2 minutos, hasta que esté humeante en el centro.
Vierte la mezcla de cordero y verduras sobre el cuscús, nivelando con una espátula.
Hornea 20 minutos, hasta que la superficie esté ligeramente dorada y crujiente.
Retira del horno, espolvorea cilantro fresco picado y sirve caliente.
tips: Si el cuscús está muy seco, humedece con una cucharada de agua antes de montar la fuente.
Puedes añadir unas almendras laminadas al final para un toque crujiente.

recipe.title: Sopa ligera de garbanzos y cuscús con carne de cordero
recipe.description: Una sopa reconfortante que reutiliza el cuscús sobrante, añadiendo garbanzos, verduras y cordero picado, perfecta para una cena ligera y digestiva.
instructions: En una olla grande, calienta 1 cda de aceite de oliva a fuego medio.
Pica la cebolla, la zanahoria y el pimiento rojo en cubos pequeños y sofríe 5 minutos, hasta que la cebolla esté dorada.

Añade el cordero picado, sazona con ½ cda de cúrcuma, 1 cda de pimentón dulce, sal y pimienta. Cocina 6 minutos, removiendo, hasta que la carne alcance 63 °C en el centro y, tras 3 minutos de reposo, se deshaga fácilmente.
Escurre y enjuaga los garbanzos de la lata, añádelos a la olla y revuelve 1 minuto.
Vierte 1 l de agua, lleva a ebullición, luego reduce a fuego medio‑bajo y cocina 10 minutos para que los sabores se integren.
Desmenuza ligeramente el cuscús sobrante con dos tenedores. Añádelo a la sopa y cocina 3 minutos más, hasta que el cuscús esté humeante en el centro.
Prueba y ajusta de sal o pimienta si es necesario.
Sirve la sopa en cuencos, espolvorea cilantro fresco picado y disfruta.
tips: Para una versión más ligera, usa solo la mitad del cordero y completa con más garbanzos.
Un chorrito de jugo de limón al servir realza el sabor sin añadir grasa.

recipe.title: Ensalada tibia de cuscús con cordero asado y verduras al grill
recipe.description: Transforma el cuscús sobrante en una ensalada tibia, combinada con cordero picado dorado y verduras asadas, ideal para una cena fresca y sin frituras.
instructions: Precalienta el grill o la plancha a fuego medio‑alto.
Corta las zanahorias en bastones finos, el pimiento rojo en tiras y la cebolla en aros gruesos.
Rocía las verduras con 2 cda de aceite de oliva, salpimienta y espolvorea ½ cda de pimentón ahumado. Asa 8 minutos, girando a la mitad, hasta que estén tiernas y ligeramente carbonizadas.

Mientras tanto, en una sartén a fuego medio, calienta 1 cda de aceite de oliva. Añade el cordero picado, sazona con 1 cda de comino, ½ cda de pimentón ahumado, sal y pimienta. Cocina 10 minutos, removiendo, hasta que la carne alcance 63 °C en el centro y, tras 3 minutos de reposo, esté bien dorada.
Desmenuza el cuscús sobrante con dos tenedores; si está muy compacto, añade una cucharada de agua tibia y mezcla hasta que quede suelto.
En un bol grande, combina el cuscús caliente, la carne de cordero dorada y las verduras asadas.
Aliña con el jugo de 1 cda de limón y el resto del aceite de oliva (1 cda). Mezcla bien.
Pica el perejil fresco y espolvorea por encima antes de servir.
Sirve la ensalada tibia en platos, acompañada de pan de pita si lo deseas.
tips: Para mayor frescura, añade unas rodajas de pepino crudo justo antes de servir.
Si el cuscús está muy seco, humedece ligeramente con agua tibia antes de mezclar.

recipe.title: Oven‑Roasted Pork Tenderloin with Dijon‑Cream Sauce and Green Beans
recipe.description: A light yet flavorful dinner featuring succulent pork tenderloin baked with a silky Dijon cream sauce, served alongside crisp green beans.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Pat the pork tenderloin dry, season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch black pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large oven‑proof skillet over medium‑high heat; sear the pork on all sides, about 2 minutes per side, until golden.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 74 °C (juices run clear).
While the pork roasts, trim the green beans and trim the ends; steam them for 6‑8 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
In a small saucepan, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat; add the finely minced 2 shallots and sauté 3 minutes, until softened and fragrant.
Stir in 2 tbsp Dijon mustard, then add the cream; bring to a gentle simmer and cook 4 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the grated 50 g Gruyère, stirring until melted and the sauce is smooth.
Rest the pork 5 minutes, then slice into 1‑cm medallions.
Plate the pork slices, drizzle with the Dijon‑cream sauce, and arrange the green beans alongside.
tips: If you prefer a crispier finish, broil the pork for the last 2 minutes.
Use a kitchen thermometer to avoid overcooking the pork.

recipe.title: Leek and Green‑Bean Velouté
recipe.description: A silky, low‑carb French‑style soup that turns leftover leeks and green beans into a comforting velouté, finished with a touch of cream.
instructions: Trim the leeks, slice them lengthwise, rinse under cold water and cut into 1‑cm rings.
Trim the green beans, cut into 2‑cm pieces.
Finely mince the shallot.
In a large pot, heat 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat; add the shallot and sauté 2 minutes, until translucent.
Add the leeks and green beans, stir, and cook 5 minutes, until the leeks begin to soften.
Pour in 800 ml water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer and cook 15 minutes, until the vegetables are very tender.
Season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch black pepper.
Using an immersion blender, puree the soup until smooth; the surface should be velvety with no visible chunks.
Stir in 5 cl cream and heat 2 minutes more, just until the soup is heated through and slightly richer.
Serve hot, optionally garnished with a drizzle of extra cream.
tips: For an even richer flavor, add a splash of dry white wine (30 ml) after sautéing the shallot.
If the soup is too thick, add a little more water until the desired consistency is reached.

recipe.title: Pan‑Seared Pork Tenderloin Medallions with Mustard‑Green‑Bean Sauté
recipe.description: Quick skillet‑cooked pork medallions paired with a tangy mustard‑green‑bean sauté, perfect for a light dinner under an hour.
instructions: Slice the pork tenderloin into 1‑cm thick medallions; season both sides with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch black pepper.
Trim the green beans and cut into 3‑cm pieces.
Finely mince the 2 shallots.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat; add the pork medallions in a single layer.
Sear 3 minutes per side, until a deep golden crust forms and the internal temperature reaches 74 °C (juices run clear). Transfer the pork to a plate and keep warm.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the butter; once melted, add the minced shallots and sauté 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the green beans, stir, and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are bright green and just tender.
Stir in 1.5 tbsp Dijon mustard, coating the beans evenly; cook 1 minute more, until the mustard is warm and glossy.
Return the pork medallions to the skillet for 1 minute just to re‑warm and pick up the sauce.
Plate the pork medallions, top with the mustard‑green‑bean sauté, and serve immediately.
tips: Do not overcrowd the pan; cook the pork in batches if necessary to obtain a proper sear.
For extra aroma, finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice (optional, not listed in pantry).
